issues.legal_issue: A tenant of qualifying land acquires occupancy-tenant status when the landlord’s disability existed when the lease was granted but had ended by the commencement of the governing code.
material_facts: The land was ryotwari land leased for cultivation to a tenant by the Court of Wards while managing the landlord’s estate.
The landlord was a minor when the lease was granted but had attained majority before the code commenced.
After the estate was released from the Court of Wards, the landlord terminated the tenancy and sued for possession and mesne profits.
The tenant held land of the kind described in the provision conferring occupancy-tenant status.
issues.conclusion: The landlord’s earlier minority did not attract the exception because the landlord was not disabled when the code commenced. The tenant acquired occupancy-tenant status at that time; the appeal was allowed and the possession suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 185(1) and 185(3) of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, 1954, a tenant holding land of the specified kind acquires occupancy-tenant status, except where the tenant holds the land from a disabled Bhumiswami. Read with sections 168(2) and 168(5), the relevant question is whether the Bhumiswami belonged to a disabled class when the Code commenced, not whether the landlord was disabled when the earlier lease was made. The Court relied on Rao Nihalkaran v. Ramgopal, [1966] 3 S.C.R. 427.

predicates.occupancy_status_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a tenant acquired statutory occupancy-tenant status in land.
predicates.tenant_held_qualifying_land_at_commencem: The tenant held land that qualified for statutory conversion to occupancy-tenant status when the governing code commenced.
predicates.landlord_disabled_at_commencement: The landlord belonged to a legally disabled class when the governing code commenced.

issues.definition: When an occupancy-status dispute concerns a tenant holding qualifying land at commencement, and the landlord was not then disabled, the tenant acquires occupancy-tenant status.
